newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso rises on "certification" volatility.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso rises on "certification" volatility.

text.p: Colombia's peso rose 4.55 pesos to 1,078.4 against the dollar in a volatile market driven by speculation over the pending U.S. "certification" decision, interbank traders said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton is due to announce whether to approve Colombia as a trustworthy ally in the drug war before the weekend or to blacklist it for a second consecutive year for its perceived failure to crack down hard enough on drug-trafficking.
Renewed decertification could trigger economic sanctions against Colombia, the United States has warned.
"Most deals were driven by speculation. The banks are looking to make a fast buck on the certification decision," a Bogota dealer said.
Dealers reported 430 operations worth a total $173 million. The peso opened at an intraday high of 1,087.35 and closed at the low.
